cards.back: The probability that a genotype produces its associated phenotype under specified conditions.
The degree or form in which a genotype-associated phenotype appears among affected individuals.
A cross to a homozygous recessive tester used to reveal the gametes produced by an individual of unknown or heterozygous genotype.
A mapping unit corresponding approximately to a 1% recombination frequency for short intervals.
A DNA sequence that influences expression of a gene on the same DNA molecule.
Restoration of a phenotype by reintroducing the implicated function after a perturbation.
Nonrandom association of alleles at different loci in a population.
Statistical and functional methods used to narrow an associated region to likely causal variants.
p = (2 n(AA) + n(Aa)) / 2N; the denominator counts allele copies.
p², 2pq, q² under random union of gametes: random mating, no selection, migration or mutation, large population, one population sampled.
F = 1 − H_obs/H_exp; one marker suggests genotyping error, many markers suggest structure or inbreeding.
q = √incidence and carriers = 2pq under Hardy–Weinberg; consanguinity biases q upward.
h² = V_A / V_P for a population in an environment; not a per-person fraction and not a measure of changeability.
h² = 2(r_MZ − r_DZ), c² = 2r_DZ − r_MZ, e² = 1 − r_MZ, assuming equal environments and additivity.
PGS = Σ β_i g_i; accuracy is variance explained in an independent sample, and r = √R².
Scores trained in one ancestry usually predict less well in others because allele frequencies and linkage differ.
Crossing to a recessive tester makes each progeny phenotype reveal the gamete from the heterozygous parent.
The rarest classes are double crossovers; the locus that differs from parental in them is the middle one.
Expected DCO = r₁ × r₂ × N; coefficient of coincidence = observed/expected; I = 1 − CoC.
Observed r undercounts multiple exchanges and cannot exceed 0.5; Haldane d = −½ ln(1 − 2r) assumes no interference.
Knockout cuts DNA; CRISPRi blocks transcription without cutting; RNAi degrades transcripts; each can hit off-targets.
Non-targeting control, two independent reagents and rescue with a resistant construct.
ΔCt = target − reference; ΔΔCt = perturbed − control; relative expression = 2^(−ΔΔCt) if efficiency ≈ 100% and the reference is stable.
Independent biological replicates are the unit; n ≈ 2(z₁ + z₂)²σ²/δ² per group is a normal approximation that runs low at small n; wells from one transfection are technical replicates.
Relevance, independence from confounders, exclusion restriction (no horizontal pleiotropy).
β_XY = β_ZY/β_ZX; SE ≈ SE(β_ZY)/|β_ZX| for strong instruments.
F ≈ (β_ZX/SE)²; below about 10 is weak and biases estimates.
MR estimates a lifelong genetic shift; check heterogeneity and robust estimators.
9:7 complementary genes; 9:3:4 recessive epistasis; 12:3:1 dominant epistasis; 15:1 duplicate genes.
Cross two recessive mutants: wild-type F1 = different genes (complement); mutant F1 = same gene.
Use counts; df = classes − 1 − estimated parameters; 5% critical values 3.84 (1 df) and 5.99 (2 df).
A double mutant resembling one single mutant suggests that gene acts downstream; daf-16 is needed for daf-2 longevity in worms.
Affected males through carrier females; never father to son; each son of a carrier mother 1/2 affected.
Posterior = prior × likelihood / Σ(prior × likelihood); prior 1/2 with three unaffected sons gives 1/9.
Each unaffected son multiplies the carrier odds by 1/2 (with complete penetrance); it lowers but does not exclude risk.
Incomplete penetrance, new mutations and X-inactivation mosaicism all change pedigree-based estimates.
MI: no normal products (2 disomic, 2 nullisomic). MII in one cell: 2 normal, 1 disomic, 1 nullisomic.
At least 5% of clinically recognized pregnancies; the leading genetic cause of pregnancy loss.
RR = risk₁/risk₀ shows strength; RD = risk₁ − risk₀ shows how many extra cases per 1000.
Near the centromere: two different parental alleles = meiosis I error; two identical alleles = meiosis II error.
Rate = events per cell division; frequency = fraction of mutant cells, inflated by early jackpots.
m = −ln(fraction of cultures with no mutants); rate ≈ m / divisions per culture.
Excess variance across independent cultures (not aliquots) shows mutations arise before selection.
Adult stem cells of several tissues gain roughly 40 mutations per year; accumulation alone does not prove causation.
CPM = gene reads / total reads × 10⁶; compare normalized values, never raw counts.
log₂(treated/control): +1 doubles, −1 halves; noisy for low-count genes.
Sort p-values; largest k with p(k) ≤ (k/m)q; call the k smallest. Controls the false discovery rate.
If a group is processed entirely in its own batch, batch and group effects cannot be separated; balance and record batches.
Mean dosage (0 to 2 effect alleles per person) divided by 2 is the effect-allele frequency.
OR = (a/b)/(c/d) from effect and other allele counts in cases and controls; χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E with 1 df.
If cases and controls differ in ancestry and allele frequencies differ by ancestry, a pooled signal can be spurious; stratify or adjust.
A multiple-testing threshold controls chance findings, not confounded ones; a corrected hit is a candidate to replicate.
PIP(i) = BF(i) / Σ BF(j) under one causal variant and equal priors; a 95% credible set sums to at least 0.95.
In heterozygotes, unequal RNA reads show something on the haplotype acts in cis; check DNA ratios and mapping bias.
Association → region; fine-mapping → candidates; chromatin → cell type; ASE → haplotype; editing → variant; rescue → phenotype in the system.
Ancestry, cell-type composition, processing batch and linkage disequilibrium must be addressed before naming a causal variant.
r = (NPD + T/2) / total tetrads: every NPD has four recombinant spores, each T has two, and each PD has none.

cards.front: PD versus NPD in unordered tetrads
cards.back: PD much greater than NPD supports linkage; this two-locus comparison alone does not determine a three-gene order.

cards.front: Sister spores in a linear four-spore ascus
cards.back: Spores 1–2 and 3–4. Meiosis I sends one dyad to each end of the ascus, and meiosis II splits each dyad in place, so its two products stay adjacent.

cards.front: First-division segregation in an eight-spore ascus
cards.back: One allele in each half (A A A A a a a a or the reverse): no exchange separated the gene from its centromere, so the alleles separated at meiosis I.

cards.front: Second-division segregation in a four-spore ascus
cards.back: Spores 1 and 2 differ: an exchange between the gene and the centromere made each dyad heterozygous, so its alleles separated at meiosis II.
r = ½ × (SDS asci ÷ total asci), so d = 50 × (SDS asci ÷ total asci) in cM. With no SDS ascus among n asci, the rule of three bounds the SDS fraction at about 3 ÷ n.

cards.front: Why the SDS estimate underestimates distant genes
cards.back: Some double exchanges restore a first-division pattern and go uncounted; with random exchanges the SDS fraction levels off near two-thirds, so the formula tops out near 33 cM.
A bacterium with F DNA integrated in its chromosome; transfer from the integrated origin can reveal chromosomal entry order in transfer-minutes.
Phage-mediated transfer in which a particle can package a random fragment of bacterial chromosomal DNA.
Frequent co-transfer of two markers supports close linkage under comparable sampling and recovery, but is not a direct base-pair distance.
A functional gene copy that restores a mutant phenotype supports a gene-function hypothesis; empty-vector and expression controls bound the claim.
Without lactose, LacI represses lac transcription; allolactose reduces repressor binding and relieves that negative control.
Low glucose raises cAMP and permits CAP activation; relieving LacI repression alone does not guarantee maximal lac output.
High tryptophan helps activate Trp repressor binding and shuts down biosynthetic genes: negative repressible control.
A mutated operator affects the linked DNA molecule; adding a diffusible repressor in trans does not repair the altered site.

cards.front: The middle marker comes from the double crossovers
cards.back: Compare each double-crossover class with the parental class it most resembles; the one marker that differs is in the middle, whatever order the table lists.

cards.front: Double crossovers: both intervals, not the outer pair
cards.back: A double crossover adds one exchange to each adjacent interval but restores the parental outer-marker combination, so the outer fraction falls short of the interval sum by twice its frequency.

cards.front: Unaffected is weaker evidence when penetrance is below 1
cards.back: Weight each genotype's prior by its probability of an unaffected phenotype and normalize; an unaffected offspring can still carry the allele.

cards.front: Does complementation establish a linear genetic map?
cards.back: No. It tests functional rescue in a shared environment; recombination addresses inherited combinations and genetic distance.

cards.front: When should a selected recombinant count be doubled?
cards.back: When it observes only one of two equally frequent reciprocal classes under the stated model; count both directly if both are observed.

cards.front: Does zero observed recombination establish zero underlying probability?
cards.back: No. Report the count and a suitable sampling interval or bound under an explicit observation model.

cards.front: Why is frame restoration weaker than proof of normal protein function?
cards.back: The intervening sequence, stops, folding or activity may still differ; measure the endpoint relevant to the claim.

cards.front: Which ratio addresses RNA abundance per genomic allele copy?
cards.back: Normalize RNA allelic odds by matched DNA allelic odds, under explicitly checked dosage and mapping assumptions.

cards.front: What makes a junction fraction interpretable as an isoform fraction?
cards.back: The observation model must specify informative counts, detection probabilities and which isoforms can contribute.

cards.front: Does an in-frame exon skip guarantee a functional protein?
cards.back: No. It can remove residues required for folding, localization, binding or catalysis; frame arithmetic alone cannot decide.

cards.front: Can aggregate skipping counts identify which homolog produced the short isoform?
cards.back: No. Allele-resolved or phase-linked transcript evidence is required, with suitable mapping controls.

cards.front: Why divide by mean fitness after selection?
cards.back: The weighted contributions describe surviving/reproducing contributions and must be normalized to frequencies before counting the next allele pool.

cards.front: Does inbreeding alone change the allele frequency in this mixture model?
cards.back: No. It redistributes genotype proportions while preserving allele counts; subsequent selection can then respond differently.

cards.front: Why calculate linkage evidence in log space?
cards.back: Products of many small probabilities can underflow; log likelihood sums retain the model comparison and make assumptions explicit.

cards.front: Can one allele-frequency snapshot identify mutation rate uniquely?
cards.back: No. Selection, dominance, migration, drift and demographic history can produce similar snapshots; additional evidence and a declared model are needed.

cards.front: Which ledgers belong in a functional-genetics report?
cards.back: The full complementation matrix, phased reciprocal haplotypes, count denominators, uncertainty assumptions and separate functional versus inherited claims.

cards.front: Why must regulatory genotype predictions track individual copies?
cards.back: Cis operators affect their linked copy while diffusible trans regulators can act on either responsive operator; total output can conceal the source.

cards.front: What does a raw one-half RNA allele fraction leave unresolved?
cards.back: Genomic dosage, mapping bias, per-copy regulation and transcript stability; matched evidence is needed for the specific contrast.

cards.front: Why is a mixture-average coding length not a transcript annotation?
cards.back: It is an expectation across distinct molecules; actual isoform sequences and their functions require separate evidence.

cards.front: What should a population simulation verify before interpretation?
cards.back: Declared life-cycle order, normalized genotype probabilities, allele accounting, boundary cases, explicit invalid states and convergence residuals.

cards.front: Why retain an exact recurrence residual alongside an approximation?
cards.back: It checks whether a proposed balance actually solves the declared life cycle; small step changes or a familiar formula alone do not establish that.
